html:
A culture of central Nigeria, known from about 1000 BCE to about the start of the common era, famous for its terracotta sculptures of human heads and figures.

The first pieces were found by tin miners near the village of Nok in 1943. The figures have large heads, finely dressed hair and eyes with pierced pupils. The Nok people were farmers and among the earliest in West Africa to smelt iron, from about the middle of the first millennium BCE. Their art is the oldest known in the region and may be linked to later work at Ife. Looting for the art market has destroyed many sites. See also the Nok people and iron in Africa.
sum: A culture of central Nigeria, known from about 1000 BCE to about the start of the common era, famous for its terracotta sculptures of human heads and figures.
